title: Larkspur Tenure and the Assisted Living Absence Waiting Period
content:
**Resident Handbook — long-standing residents and the absence-relief credit of the Assisted Living Residency and Care Agreement.**

Larkspur tenure shortens the waiting midnights of the absence-relief credit, never below zero.

**Where tenure starts.** Tenure is counted in whole months up to the handling date from the move-in date of the customer's Larkspur independent living residency — the residency under the Independent Living Residency Agreement — when the assisted living admission came from Larkspur independent living, and otherwise from the assisted living move-in date.

**Whole months.** A whole month is completed each time the count reaches the same day of the month as the starting date; a hypothetical tenure starting on 15 March 2021 completes 60 whole months on 15 March 2026 and has 59 whole months on 14 March 2026.

**How much shorter.**

| Larkspur tenure on the handling date | Waiting midnights shortened by |
|---|---|
| At least 60 whole months | 3 midnights |
| At least 24 but under 60 whole months | 1 midnight |
| Under 24 whole months | No shortening |

### Cases (hypothetical residents)

- Moved into Larkspur independent living in January 2019, then into assisted living from that residency in 2024; handling date in March 2026: tenure counts from the independent living move-in, more than 60 whole months — waiting midnights shortened by 3, so a waiting of 10 midnights becomes 7.
- Moved into assisted living from home 30 months before the handling date: at least 24 but under 60 — shortened by 1, so a waiting of 14 midnights becomes 13.
- Moved into assisted living from home 23 whole months before the handling date: no shortening.
- Tenure of exactly 24 whole months: shortened by 1; exactly 60 whole months: shortened by 3.
